answer: A durable defense is a refundable identity bond: every agent must lock stake before it can earn, like a crystal-clear deposit held in escrow. Creating a hundred fake identities then costs a hundred bonds, while honest agents get theirs back. A narrow inlet of cheap entry invites floods, so the bond should scale with the rewards an identity can claim, and proven duplicates lose the stake. This turns Sybil from a free copy-paste trick into a priced gamble: attackers pay real capital per identity, and the system can raise the bond when shale-like layers of cheap clones appear.
